analysis: SandboxEligibility.swift: the sizing logic moved from the Swift eligibility struct to a SandboxSizingPlan type that the add-on reports, with estimatedPlan as the fallback. This is display and sizing logic only. There is no new I/O, privilege or crypto, and the arithmetic uses Int64 with clamps. A plan reported by a hostile installer could mislead the owner about sizing, but the provider's attestation, keys and the inference path are not touched. SandboxInstaller.swift: adds a --plan option, supportsPlan (a substring match on untrusted script text), and planArguments (no --yes). Slot arguments are Int-formatted, so there is no argument injection. The HTTPS-only download, size limit and owner-only staging are unchanged. The one security-relevant change is ordering: the downloaded installer is now run before the consent prompt, which is the finding above (TB-013/T-061). SandboxSetupCommand.swift has no text in the supplied units, only metadata and a truncated patch excerpt. I could not verify how the --plan output (JSON progress) is parsed, how the plan process is sandboxed or what environment it gets, whether failures fall back safely to estimatedPlan, or whether any plan field flows into a command or path. The setvbuf line-buffering change is benign. No inference-path, App Attest or provider-key changes. A deeper review should cover the full SandboxSetupCommand.swift and the parsing of the plan output.

findings.detail: SandboxInstaller.planArguments/supportsPlan (head lines 102-123) and the updated setup discussion in SandboxSetupCommand.swift say setup downloads install.sh and "asks it for the add-on's plan" before it "explains what changes and asks before installing anything". Previously the script ran only after consent. Now the remote script runs as the Mac owner before any approval. The only gate on running it is a substring check of the script's own text for "--plan", and the script is not verified at that point (the release checks happen inside the installer). A misissued certificate or compromised sandbox service could serve a script that executes its payload regardless of the flag, and the owner's confirmation no longer prevents it. Fix: run the plan step only after consent, or compute the plan from a signed or verified data source rather than by executing the downloaded script. Otherwise state in TB-013/T-061 that the script runs before consent, and keep that run sandboxed with a minimal environment.
findings.title: Downloaded installer script is now executed (--plan) before the owner approves any install
